name: Shelomith
overview: Shelomith was a female member of the tribe of Dan known primarily as the mother of an unnamed man who cursed the Name of God. Her identity is briefly mentioned in the context of this significant event recorded in Leviticus 24:11. Beyond this, Scripture provides limited information about her life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Shelomith means 'at peace' in Hebrew. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaning that reflects tranquility or harmony.
familyAndRelationships: Shelomith is explicitly identified as the daughter of Dibri. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for her beyond being the mother of the man who cursed the Name of God.
scriptureSignificance: Shelomith's significance in the biblical narrative arises from her association with her son, who committed the grave offense of cursing the Name of God. This incident highlights the seriousness of blasphemy and the holiness of God's Name in Israelite society. Her mention serves to identify the lineage and tribal affiliation connected to this noteworthy event.
